summary: The article provides a largely accurate and comprehensive overview of Video-KYC (V-CIP) in India, aligning well with RBI guidelines and current practices.

claims.claim: Video-KYC, officially known as the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP), is a smart way to complete your "Know Your Customer" (KYC) verification without stepping out of your home.
claims.note: V-CIP is defined as an alternate method of customer identification with facial recognition and customer due diligence by an authorised official of the RE by undertaking seamless, secure, live, informed-consent based audio-visual interaction with the customer to obtain identification information required for CDD purpose, and to ascertain the veracity of the information furnished by the customer through independent verification and maintaining audit trail of the process.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has consistently encouraged the adoption of the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) by financial institutions through various circulars and updates to its Master Direction on KYC.
claims.note: The RBI introduced V-CIP through an amendment to its Master Direction on KYC on January 9, 2020, and has since updated it multiple times, including significant amendments in May 2021 and subsequent updates.

claims.claim: The official will capture your photo, verify your identity by comparing your face to your document photo, and perform "liveness detection" to ensure it's really you. They will also cross-check details with official databases like the Aadhaar database.
claims.note: RBI guidelines for V-CIP explicitly mention that the official must conduct liveness checks, detect fraudulent attempts, match the photograph and details on Aadhaar/OVD and PAN/e-PAN with the customer, and verify information through independent means.

claims.claim: You typically need your original PAN card and Aadhaar card (or other valid address proof) ready during the call, as the official will need to see and verify them.
claims.note: During a V-CIP call, customers are required to show their original Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) like PAN and Aadhaar to the camera for verification.

claims.claim: It's increasingly available for opening savings accounts, fixed deposits, credit cards, and some loan applications. However, the specific services offered via V-CIP can vary from bank to bank and financial institution to institution.
claims.note: V-CIP can be used for onboarding new individual customers, proprietors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners of legal entities, converting existing minimum KYC accounts, and for periodic updation of KYC records.

claims.claim: Yes, you can do it from any location with a stable internet connection and good lighting, as long as you are physically present in India and the location is private enough for you to share personal details securely.
claims.note: RBI guidelines mandate that customers must be physically present in India during Video KYC, and systems use geo-tagging technology to verify the customer's Indian location.

article_title: Your Bank Accounts Just Got Easier to Open: Understanding Video-KYC
